jobs.description:
About Kaseya

Kaseya is the leading provider of AI-powered IT management and cybersecurity software, serving Managed Service Providers (MSPs) and internal IT organizations worldwide. Our comprehensive platform helps organizations efficiently manage, secure, and automate their IT environments, driving operational efficiency and long-term business success.

Backed by Insight Partners , a leading global software investor, Kaseya has experienced sustained double-digit growth and continues to expand its global footprint. Today, Kaseya supports customers in more than 20 countries and manages over 15 million endpoints worldwide.

Founded in 2000, Kaseya was built by builders - and we're still building. We look for people who create rather than wait, who see a hard problem and lean in, and who treat challenges as raw material. At Kaseya, everyone plays a role in shaping the future of IT: whether you're in engineering, product, sales, marketing, customer support, or operations, your work helps protect, defend, and optimize IT environments across the globe.

We're building teams that grow, perform, and make an impact. If you're driven by the itch to make things better - a product, a process, a career - you'll fit right in.

At Kaseya, we don't just raise the bar. We build it.

We are seeking a detail-oriented, hands-on Product Analyst to join our Business Information Systems (BIS) team. Working closely with the Product Manager, this individual will be responsible for defining, documenting, testing, and delivering enterprise capabilities supporting our Product Business Systems (PBS), the internal systems that support our Product organization, focusing on two main areas: business systems’ products and pricing, and software provisioning, usage, and overage.

This role will support both Kaseya’s current operating environment and its future-state transformation. PBS is a newly formed team and growing fast! PBS capabilities are supported across platforms including Salesforce, NetSuite, integrations, and our Kaseya products, including Kaseya One.

As Kaseya advances its transformation, this role will help support the transition to a more scalable future-state architecture anchored by Salesforce Revenue Cloud Advanced (RCA), Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Oracle ERP, and related boundary applications.

The ideal candidate will understand how the Lead-to-Cash process works at an Enterprise SaaS company and will be comfortable turning business needs into detailed Jira stories, acceptance criteria, and test cases. Hands-on exposure to configuring Products and Pricing, bundle configurations, and provisioning software licenses through different integration tools (MuleSoft, Boomi, etc.) and capturing usage and overage in different systems (Salesforce and NetSuite) is strongly preferred.

This person must be comfortable operating in a fast-paced, dynamic environment with competing priorities, while helping Kaseya simplify legacy processes, strengthen controls, and deliver well-tested, well-documented PBS capabilities for the future.

Product & Pricing Capabilities in Scope:

- Product Configuration: Product configuration using the Revenue Cloud configurator, Product attribute selection and validation.

- Product Catalog Management: Product creation and onboarding, SKU management, Product hierarchy management, Product master data governance, Oracle synchronization.

- Product Governance: Product intake process, data dictionary management, Integration dependency documentation, revenue recognition and billing metadata

- Pricing Management Capabilities: Pricing Waterfall, Discount Management, Renewal Pricing, Dynamic Pricing, Pricing Governance, Promotions

- Bundle Management Capabilities: Bundle Modeling, Configuration, Ownership Validation, Cart Management, Cross-sell/Upsell, Bundle Pricing

Fulfillment & Provisioning Capabilities in Scope:

- Provisioning Method Management: Automated provisioning, Manual provisioning, Hybrid provisioning, Fulfillment route determination, Platform selection (K1, DPP, Manual Operations)

- Provisioning Exception Management: Provisioning Error Handling, Manual Provisioning, Provisioning Operations

- Tenant & Instance Provisioning: New tenant provisioning, Tenant onboarding, Customer-to-tenant mapping, Multi-tenant support, Instance Management, Instance creation, Instance updates, Instance identity management, Zone and sub-domain assignment

- Entitlement Management: License Provisioning, Entitlement Lifecycle Management

- Usage & Rating: Support for subscription, usage-based, hardware, and one-time products; usage consumption and rating; overage management; and related billing and revenue treatment.

Key Responsibilities:

- Business Requirements & Analysis

- Elicit, analyze, and document business requirements for Product and Pricing, Fulfillment & Provisioning capabilities in support of the roadmap set by the Product Manager

- Develop deep working knowledge of PBS processes and data across current and future-state systems, including Salesforce, Salesforce Revenue Cloud Advanced, NetSuite, Oracle ERP, MuleSoft / Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC), Kaseya One, and key boundary applications.

- Partner with Finance, Billing Operations, Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, Customer Operations, Product, Engineering, Architecture, Security, and IT stakeholders to gather requirements, clarify business rules, and validate that delivered solutions meet the stated need.

- Produce and maintain business requirements documents (BRDs), functional specifications, process flows, data mappings, and decision logs that serve as the source of truth for PBS workstreams.

- Perform gap analysis between current-state (legacy) and future-state processes, documenting impacts, dependencies, and migration-readiness considerations for the Product Manager and Architecture teams.

- Support the Product Manager in maturing the PBS operating model by documenting as-is and to-be processes, clarifying ownership and handoffs, and identifying manual steps that can be eliminated or automated.

- Apply business acumen and knowledge of managed service providers (MSPs), subscription-based business models, usage-based billing, customer lifecycle processes, and Corporate / BIS systems.

- Lead-to-Cash Lifecycle Execution

- Own detailed requirements definition and traceability across the Lead-to-Cash (L2C) lifecycle, with a focus on product and pricing setup, order fulfillment and provisioning, entitlements, and usage and overage capture, including downstream impacts on billing, revenue recognition, and reporting.

- Translate complex business processes into clear system requirements, Jira epics and user stories, acceptance criteria, process flows, and testable outcomes.

- Validate that product, pricing, order, entitlement, provisioning, and usage data flows are consistent, traceable, and aligned across integrated systems, performing data analysis and reconciliation where needed.

- Partner with technical teams to document and test integrations between Salesforce, NetSuite, Kaseya One and the rest of the products.

- Jira & Agile Delivery

- Maintain the Jira backlog day-to-day: write clear, actionable user stories and acceptance criteria; keep epics, stories, sub-tasks, labels, components, and fix versions accurate and up to date.

- Prepare and facilitate backlog refinement, participate in sprint planning, daily stand-ups, solution reviews, demos, and retrospectives for assigned PBS workstreams; ensure stories are groomed and ready before sprint start.

- Track story status, defects, and blockers in Jira; produce sprint and release reporting (burndown, velocity, defect counts) for the Product Manager and stakeholders.

- Partner with Scrum Masters, Engineering Leads, QA, Business Process Leads, and Release / PMO teams to clarify requirements, resolve open questions quickly, and keep work flowing through the sprint.

- Support delivery across both business-as-usual (BAU) and NextGen (future-state transformation) workstreams, keeping Jira work clearly tagged and separated between legacy support, transformation delivery, and migration-readiness activities.

- Cross-Functional Collaboration

- Work closely with technical leads, engineers, QA, enterprise architecture, fulfillment operations, finance operations and customer support teams to deliver end-to-end solutions.

- Act as a liaison between business users and technical teams, translating operational pain points and business needs into detailed system requirements and answering functional questions during build.

- Document impacts to upstream and downstream teams and confirm they are understood and signed off before changes are introduced into production.

- Triage and support issue resolution across complex, integrated workflows, reproducing issues, gathering evidence, and logging clear defect tickets where ownership spans multiple teams, platforms, or business functions.

- Governance, Risk & Compliance

- Ensure requirements and test coverage address applicable compliance standards, including internal controls, data privacy, and security requirements.

- Partner with governance, architecture, security, integration, and release management teams to maintain alignment with enterprise policies.

- Ensure every change is backed by clear documentation, approved requirements, defined business rules, traceable decisions, test evidence, and operational readiness artifacts (release notes, training materials, runbooks).

- UAT & Quality Assurance

- Define test strategy and write detailed test cases and scripts (functional, regression, integration, and end-to-end) that trace directly back to requirements and acceptance criteria.

- Plan, coordinate, and execute User Acceptance Testing (UAT) with business users across Finance, Billing, Revenue Operations, and Fulfillment; prepare test data, track UAT progress, and obtain formal business sign-off.

- Log, triage, and prioritize defects in Jira; partner with QA and Engineering on root-cause analysis, retesting, and closure, and report defect trends and quality metrics to the Product Manager.

- Validate post-release behavior in production (hypercare), monitor data quality and defect trends, and feed findings back into the backlog to continuously improve PBS capabilities.

Required Qualifications:

- 5+ years of experience as a Product Analyst, Business Analyst, or Business Systems Analyst supporting CRM, ERP, billing, or revenue operations systems in an enterprise SaaS environment.

- Solid understanding of Lead-to-Cash, Quote-to-Cash, or subscription lifecycle processes.

- Hands-on experience writing and managing Jira epics, user stories, acceptance criteria, and defects; proficiency with Jira and Confluence (JQL, boards, dashboards) strongly preferred.

- Demonstrated experience writing test cases, executing functional and regression testing, and planning and running UAT cycles with business users through to sign-off.

- Working knowledge of Salesforce CPQ, Salesforce Revenue Cloud / RCA, NetSuite, integration platforms (MuleSoft, Boomi), or comparable enterprise systems; exposure to software license provisioning, entitlements, and usage-based pricing is a plus.

- Understanding of integrated system flows across sales, order management, billing, receivables, collections, revenue recognition, and reporting.

- Experience working within Agile/Scrum teams on enterprise-scale system implementations; comfortable facilitating refinement and participating in all sprint ceremonies.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills; able to run requirements workshops, document decisions clearly, and work effectively with both business users and engineers.

- Solid understanding of business process mapping, technical integrations, data dependencies, and system controls; basic SQL or data analysis skills for validating data across systems preferred.

- Highly organized and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams and navigate a mix of legacy and future-state platforms.

Why Join Us?

This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to critical initiatives at the intersection of products, technology, and enterprise transformation. You will help define, test, and deliver how Kaseya manages the Lead-to-Cash lifecycle today while building the scalable future-state systems and processes needed to support growth, automation and stronger controls. You’ll work with a high-performing team, grow your expertise across a modern enterprise systems landscape, and see your work go live with real business impact. We also make sure we have fun along the way!

Position Summary

The Product Manager, Order to Cash will own the strategy, roadmap, and execution of Kaseya’s end-to-end Order-to-Cash (O2C) product capabilities, including order management, billing, invoicing, payments, cash application, collections, revenue recognition, tax, and reporting.

This role will serve as the product subject matter expert for the O2C lifecycle and partner closely with Finance, Billing, Collections, Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, Customer Operations, Product, Engineering, Architecture, Security, and IT to simplify complex processes, improve the customer experience, strengthen financial controls, and enable scalable growth.

The ideal candidate combines strong product management discipline with deep O2C expertise and is comfortable operating across business processes, enterprise applications, data, and integrations. This individual will translate complex business needs into clear product priorities and scalable solutions while identifying opportunities for automation, process optimization, and technology transformation.

Key Responsibilities

- Define and execute the O2C product strategy and roadmap across order management, billing, invoicing, payments, collections, revenue recognition, tax, and reporting.

- Own and prioritize the O2C product backlog based on business value, customer impact, operational efficiency, financial requirements, risk, and Kaseya’s broader transformation strategy.

- Serve as the primary O2C product subject matter expert and trusted advisor to business and technology stakeholders.

- Translate complex business processes and customer needs into clear product requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, process flows, and measurable outcomes.

- Own the product experience across the complete O2C lifecycle, from order creation and validation through invoicing, payment, cash application, collections, revenue recognition, and financial reporting.

- Partner with Finance, Billing, Collections, Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, and Customer Operations to improve end-to-end O2C processes and business outcomes.

- Support O2C processes across Kaseya’s direct sales, ecommerce, partner/channel, and EDI business models.

- Support subscription, usage-based, consolidated, and customer-specific billing models, including invoice generation, credit memos, refunds, disputes, adjustments, write-offs, and customer inquiries.

- Define product requirements for payment processing, authorization, settlement, tokenization, autopay, refunds, chargebacks, ACH, wires, lockbox, and cash application.

- Partner with Finance and Accounting to support revenue recognition, contract assets and liabilities, journal posting, ARR reporting, revenue reporting, and financial controls.

- Support credit and collections capabilities, including dunning, payment follow-up, disputes, write-offs, bad debt, and credit management.

- Support tax calculation, exemptions, invoice and credit-memo tax treatment, e-invoicing, auditability, and related compliance requirements.

- Partner with Engineering, Architecture, IT, and technical teams to design and deliver scalable solutions across Kaseya’s O2C technology ecosystem.

- Manage product requirements, dependencies, integrations, and data flows across platforms including Salesforce, Salesforce Revenue Cloud, Oracle ERP/Fusion, NetSuite, RightRev, GetPaid, Gr4vy, GoCardless, OneSource, Snowflake, MuleSoft, Oracle Integration Cloud, and related applications.

- Ensure critical O2C data, including orders, invoices, payments, customers, tax, receivables, and revenue, remains accurate, traceable, and consistently synchronized across systems.

- Partner with technical teams to establish appropriate controls for security, privacy, auditability, data governance, and regulatory compliance.

- Lead product initiatives supporting the evolution of Kaseya’s O2C operating model and technology landscape.

- Support the migration of legacy NetSuite O2C capabilities into Kaseya’s evolving Salesforce and Oracle ecosystem while maintaining business continuity.

- Identify opportunities to standardize processes, improve cross-functional handoffs, eliminate manual work, and reduce operational risk.

- Balance investment in existing platforms with longer-term transformation and migration priorities, prioritizing initiatives that deliver measurable business value.

- Establish product KPIs and success measures to evaluate operational performance, automation, data quality, customer experience, and financial impact.

- Identify opportunities to leverage automation and AI to improve billing, collections, dispute management, and other O2C processes.

Required Qualifications

- 5+ years of experience in product management, business systems, enterprise applications, or a related discipline, with significant experience owning Order-to-Cash products or capabilities.

- Deep understanding of end-to-end O2C processes, including order management, billing, invoicing, payments, cash application, collections, revenue recognition, and financial reporting.

- Experience supporting subscription-based, SaaS, usage-based, or recurring revenue business models.

- Demonstrated experience translating complex business processes into product requirements, roadmaps, user stories, and scalable technology solutions.

- Experience working with enterprise ERP, CRM, billing, payment, or revenue-management platforms.

- Strong understanding of enterprise integrations, APIs, data flows, and dependencies across business applications.

- Experience leading cross-functional initiatives involving Finance, Accounting, Sales, Operations, Engineering, IT, and other business stakeholders.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to understand complex systems and translate them into practical solutions.

- Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to influence decisions across both business and technical teams.

- Experience with digital transformation, systems migration, process optimization, and automation initiatives.

- Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, highly cross-functional environment with competing priorities.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience in a SaaS, MSP, technology, or high-growth environment.

- Experience with Salesforce Revenue Cloud, Oracle ERP/Fusion, NetSuite, RightRev, GetPaid, Gr4vy, GoCardless, OneSource, MuleSoft, Oracle Integration Cloud, or Snowflake.

- Experience with AI-enabled automation within Finance, Billing, Collections, or O2C processes.

- Experience operating in a global environment with multiple business models, geographies, currencies, tax jurisdictions, and payment methods.

- Experience leading large-scale ERP, CRM, billing, payments, revenue management, or O2C transformation initiatives.

- Experience working within a complex enterprise technology environment with multiple interconnected systems and integrations.

- Experience in a private equity-backed or high-growth organization.

Additional information

This role reports to the SVP, Growth & Product Strategy, within the CTO's organization. It's a rare seat: a new capability with executive sponsorship and the room to build it from the ground up.

This role will build and own a scalable, rapid voice-of-customer engine for Growth & Product Strategy and will define who we talk to, how quickly we can reach them, and how what we learn feeds the company's most important product and growth decisions. This person establishes the methods, customer access, toolkit, and operating cadence that get the team to trustworthy answers in days and weeks rather than months.

This role runs discovery interviews for priority segments while building the process, codifying what works into playbooks, and raising the bar on rigor across the Product org. Rather than standing up an expensive, heavyweight research function, they find fast, creative ways to surface insight, leveraging disparate sources across the company, from sales and customer success to support tickets.

A core part of the mandate is partnership across Product and Go-To-Market. This role brings user insight into product discovery early and often, partnering with Product to ensure that roadmap bets are grounded in real customer need rather than opinion. With GTM teams (marketing, sales, and customer success) they help turn customer truth into sharper positioning, messaging, and segmentation, and tap those teams as a fast channel to customers already in the field. Across both, this role operates credibly at senior levels, translating research into strategic direction leaders can act on.

Key Responsibilities

- Build the rapid voice-of-customer engine. Leveraging existing and new customer feedback channels, design and stand up a repeatable process for reaching not just today’s customers but prospects and new segments in days and weeks, not months — defining who we talk to, how we reach them fast, which method fits each question, and how findings flow into product, GTM, and segment decisions. Own the research stack and budget, investing where the questions justify it.

- Own creative, fast customer access. Build and maintain the panels and channels that reach the right MSP and Direct IT customers and end users on short notice, spanning quick calls, discovery and usability interviews, expert networks, in-product experiences, win/loss reviews, and events like webinars and Product Councils, and mobilize the people already talking to customers every day, from sales to customer success.

- Partner with Product and GTM to drive the decisions that matter. Embed user insight in product discovery, pressure-test roadmap bets against real customer needs, and give teams the evidence to prioritize with confidence, so the org builds and goes to market on what matters, not what shouts loudest.

- Turn raw input into decision-ready insight and strategy. Synthesize what customers say and do into clear, honest findings on unmet needs, usage friction, buying behavior, churn drivers, and expansion opportunities, framed to inform a specific decision, not to sit in a report. Bring that point of view directly into strategy conversations with senior leaders, and challenge assumptions when the evidence warrants.

- Make the capability scalable. Create the frameworks, playbooks, templates, and best practices that let others across Product and GTM run good customer research without this role in the room.

Key Requirements

- A product manager's mindset, whether or not you've carried the title. You frame research around the decision it serves, think in terms of outcomes and prioritization, and have the product judgment to help teams decide what to build, not just report what you heard.

- 8+ years in Product Management, Strategy, Customer or User Research, or Insights, or a comparable role centered on getting to customer truth and putting it to work, including demonstrated experience embedding in product discovery, informing roadmap prioritization, and building or scaling a research capability rather than only running individual studies.

- Range across altitude and context. You move fluidly from a feature-level detail to the strategic and competitive landscape, and you've seen enough different businesses and models to bring pattern recognition rather than a single playbook.

- Fluent across a broad method set, qualitative and quantitative, including discovery and usability interviews, surveys, expert networks, in-product research and experimentation, win/loss, and behavioral or product data, with the judgment to match method to question and make the right speed-versus-rigor call.

- A builder who shapes strategy, not just findings. Track record of building or scaling a research process, function, or panel — and the tools and vendor relationships behind it — paired with the ability to connect customer truth to where the business should play and how it wins, moving product and GTM strategy rather than only informing it.

- A persuasive communicator who changes minds. You structure a case so the recommendation leads and the logic underneath it holds (top-down, decision-first) and you hold your own with a skeptical senior audience, even when the evidence challenges what people want to hear.

What Success Looks Like

- A standing voice-of-customer engine reliably answers the team's priority questions in days and weeks rather than months.

- The right MSP and Direct IT customers are reachable on short notice, with panels, expert networks, and research tools live and in regular use.

- Customer insight consistently shows up in real decisions, informing product priorities, GTM choices, and customer segmentation.

- Customer truth shows up in strategy, not just execution, shaping where the business chooses to play and how it wins, and changing at least some senior bets that would otherwise have gone on instinct.

- The process is repeatable and documented, quality holds as volume grows, and others run research well using the frameworks and playbooks this role creates.

- Speed and rigor stay balanced: useful answers land quickly and sharpen as more evidence comes in.

This is a rare opportunity to build the customer-truth engine at the heart of a new strategic capability, with direct exposure to senior leadership, a hand in the company's most important growth questions, and the room to build it your way .
